```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5)
set.seed(123)
```

## 1. Question and data

**Question:** which genomic regions are associated with grain yield and
flowering time (anthesis) in maize?

**Data:** the public DROPS dataset shipped with the `statgenGWAS` package
(European DROPS project): 246 maize genotypes, about 42,000 SNP markers with
chromosome positions, and phenotypes measured in several field trials. This
analysis uses trial `Mur13W`.

```{r libs}
library(statgenGWAS)
library(ggplot2)
```

## 2. Build the genomic data object

```{r gdata}
data("dropsMarkers")
data("dropsMap")
data("dropsPheno")

# Genotype names as row names, drop the helper column
rownames(dropsMarkers) <- dropsMarkers[["Ind"]]
dropsMarkers <- dropsMarkers[colnames(dropsMarkers) != "Ind"]

# Marker map: SNP names as row names, standard column names
rownames(dropsMap) <- dropsMap[["SNP.names"]]
colnames(dropsMap)[match(c("Chromosome", "Position"),
                         colnames(dropsMap))] <- c("chr", "pos")

# Phenotypes: one data.frame per trial
colnames(dropsPheno)[colnames(dropsPheno) == "Variety_ID"] <- "genotype"
dropsPhenoList <- split(
  x = dropsPheno[c("genotype", "grain.yield", "grain.number", "seed.size",
                   "anthesis", "silking", "plant.height",
                   "tassel.height", "ear.height")],
  f = dropsPheno[["Experiment"]])

gDataDrops <- createGData(geno = dropsMarkers, map = dropsMap,
                          pheno = dropsPhenoList)
```

## 3. Marker quality control

`codeMarkers` removes duplicate SNPs and markers with too many missing values.

```{r qc}
gDataDropsDedup <- codeMarkers(gDataDrops, impute = FALSE, verbose = TRUE)
summary(gDataDropsDedup)
```

## 4. Phenotype distributions

```{r pheno}
pheno <- gDataDropsDedup$pheno[["Mur13W"]]
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
hist(pheno$grain.yield, breaks = 25, col = "grey70",
     main = "Grain yield (Mur13W)", xlab = "grain.yield")
hist(pheno$anthesis, breaks = 25, col = "grey70",
     main = "Anthesis (Mur13W)", xlab = "anthesis")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

## 5. Single-trait GWAS

`runSingleTraitGwas` fits a linear mixed model with a kinship matrix to account
for relatedness between genotypes, which reduces false positives caused by
population structure.

```{r gwas}
GWASDrops <- runSingleTraitGwas(gData = gDataDropsDedup,
                                trials = "Mur13W",
                                traits = c("grain.yield", "anthesis"))
summary(GWASDrops)
```

## 6. QQ plots

If the model controls population structure, p-values should follow the diagonal
except for a few true associations at the tail.

```{r qq}
plot(GWASDrops, plotType = "qq", trait = "grain.yield")
plot(GWASDrops, plotType = "qq", trait = "anthesis")
```

## 7. Manhattan plots

```{r manhattan}
plot(GWASDrops, plotType = "manhattan", trait = "grain.yield")
plot(GWASDrops, plotType = "manhattan", trait = "anthesis")
```

## 8. Significant SNPs across traits

```{r qtl}
plot(GWASDrops, plotType = "qtl", yThr = 4, normalize = TRUE)
```

## 9. Export results

```{r export}
dir.create("results", showWarnings = FALSE)
res <- GWASDrops$GWAResult[["Mur13W"]]
if (!is.null(res)) {
  write.csv(res, "results/gwas_Mur13W_all_snps.csv", row.names = FALSE)
}
names(GWASDrops)
head(res)
```

## 10. Limitations

- 246 genotypes and a single trial give limited power; small-effect loci are
  likely missed.
- Significant SNPs are candidate regions, not proven causal variants. Validating
  them would need independent data or functional work.
- Results come from one trial; effects can change across environments.
